Atacama Hyalella · cox1 · preliminary v1

Which Hyalella lineages are our samples, and where do their closest known relatives live?

We compared one mitochondrial gene (cox1) from 40 of our amphipods with 1,021 public Hyalella sequences.

Five findings

  1. All 40 of our 40 samples match lineages already in the public databases (every one is at least 97% identical to a known sequence). No new lineage shows up at cox1.
  2. 21 PCR samples are Andean. Their closest known relatives come from the high Andes of Argentina and Peru.
  3. 9 PCR samples and all 10 genome samples match the North American Hyalella azteca group. That is unexpected for the Atacama.
  4. Check those North American matches before interpreting them. Sample mix-up, lab-culture contamination or an introduced population are all possible.
  5. Confidence: high for which group each sample is in, low for how the groups relate. Only 2 of 1,021 public Hyalella cox1 records are from Chile, so "closest known" is limited by what others have sequenced.

Full explanation and caveats: report.md
